speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you have been experiencing rectal bleeding and if you have noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or constipation?

speaker: Patient
text: 45-year-old female. The patient reports a 2-week history of rectal bleeding occurring daily with bowel movements. She denies any pain with defecation and does not present with any other complaints.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any family history of colorectal cancer or inflammatory bowel disease? Have you experienced any unintentional weight loss or changes in stool caliber, such as pencil-thin stools?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rectal bleeding daily with bowel movements. I also have No pain with defecation.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will perform a digital rectal exam to better characterize the palpable mass and check for any other abnormalities. REQUEST TEST: Colonoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal colonoscopy, I suspect the bleeding originates from a lesion within the anal canal, such as an anal canal tumor or severe hemorrhoids. REQUEST TEST: Anoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: The anoscopy reveals internal hemorrhoids, which are a common cause of painless rectal bleeding. Given the palpable mass and the patient's age, I must rule out other pathologies like anal cancer or rectal prolapse despite the normal colonoscopy. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRI rules out deep pelvic masses or advanced anal cancer, which is reassuring. Since the anoscopy confirmed internal hemorrhoids and they are the most likely source of the painless bleeding, I am confident in this diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Internal Hemorrhoids
